text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew honoured as an "Architect of the New Century" in Washington, D.C., by Nixn Center for Peace and Freedom.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore acts to tighten controls at listed companies and raise standards of corporate governance.
- National University of Singapore lecturer who made remarks described as religiously offensive and racist during recent university talk reprimanded by university.
- Closely watched indicator of US semiconductor demand stages strong recovery but many analysts unconvinced it signals sustained recovery.
- Housing Development Board resale market seems to have escaped relatively unscathed from government curbs on property speculation introduced in May.
- Kian Ann Engineering marks debut with stunning premium, rising as much as 65 percent to 99 cents.
- Electronics sector rises to 17-week high on news of recovery in U.S. book-to-bill ratio, but observers cautious about industry's medium-term outlook.
- Billionaire Li Ka-shing indicates plans to shift to a lower gear from 1998 and leave huge business empire to younger managers.
- Tuan Sing Holdings agrees to buy majority stake in large Shelford Road property project privately owned by Cam International chairman Raymond Chew Chuan Seng.
- Property counters up as investors feel worst is over for residential property sector and the economy.
- Alliance Securities revises upwards its earnings growth forecast for Big Four banks from 12 to 13 percent, compared with last year's 10 percent.
- Computer hitch halts Stock Exchange of Singapore trading 35 minutes early on Tuesday.
